spec.name: def_lowvol_pure
spec.note: Canonical low-volatility anomaly as a standalone ranking. Train rank IC is NEGATIVE (t60=-5.1), so a positive train edge is NOT expected; the test is whether the sign flips out of sample when high-beta unwinds.

spec.name: def_lottery_skew
spec.note: Anti-lottery leg of the low-risk anomaly (MAX effect) plus negative-skew avoidance. Only 0.43 rank-correlated with each other and 0.56/0.37 with low_vol, so this is a partly independent defensive signal. Same exit as 01/03/04 so the factor is isolated.

spec.name: def_lowbeta_pure
spec.note: Betting-against-beta leg. Least correlated with low_vol of the defensive set (rank corr 0.40) and the least negative on train (t60=-1.8), so it is the least ruled-out member of the family. idio_vol is deliberately omitted: it is 0.99 rank-correlated with low_vol and would be a duplicate test.

spec.name: def_composite
spec.note: All four defensive legs combined: low vol, low beta, anti-lottery, negative-skew avoidance. Weights set by rank-correlation (low_vol full weight, the partly independent legs downweighted), not fitted. Exit identical to 01/02/03 so selection is the only thing that varies.

spec.name: def_composite_timeonly
spec.note: Same selection as 04 but with no stop and no trail at all: pure 60-session hold. The low-risk anomaly is a buy-and-hold claim, and an ATR stop on a calm stock is a noise-tight stop. Paired with 04 this separates 'defensive selection failed' from 'the exit policy failed'.

spec.name: def_lowvol_universe
spec.note: Defensive as a risk CONSTRAINT rather than a ranking: hard-cap the universe at 0.30 annualised vol (the calm ~37% of names, ~106 per scan, ~76 after the 200DMA filter) and rank on trend within it. This is how low-vol is implemented in practice and is the alternative hypothesis to 01-05 - that defensive pays as a filter on trend, not as a stock-picking signal.

spec.name: def_cap025
spec.note: ROBUSTNESS, pre-registered: identical to def_lowvol_universe but a tighter 0.25 vol cap (~51 names/scan). If the defensive cap is real the neighbourhood should hold; if only 0.30 works it is noise.

spec.name: def_cap035
spec.note: ROBUSTNESS, pre-registered: identical to def_lowvol_universe but a looser 0.35 vol cap (~159 names/scan). Neighbour on the other side of 0.30.

spec.name: def_cap_only
spec.note: ATTRIBUTION: the 0.30 vol cap alone, with the 200DMA trend filter REMOVED. Isolates the defensive component of def_lowvol_universe. Paired with def_200dma_only this says whether the low-risk filter or the trend filter produced the out-of-sample flip.

spec.name: def_200dma_only
spec.note: ATTRIBUTION CONTROL: the 200DMA trend filter alone, with NO vol cap. Contains zero defensive content. If this matches def_lowvol_universe out of sample then the defensive filter added nothing and the family is dead.

spec.name: def_lowvol_universe_60d
spec.note: EXIT ROBUSTNESS, pre-registered: same selection as def_lowvol_universe, wider stop and longer hold (3.0 ATR / trail 4.0 / 60 sessions). If the edge only exists at one exit setting it is noise.

spec.name: def_calm_universe_defrank
spec.note: Same calm universe as def_lowvol_universe (0.30 vol cap + 200DMA) but ranked by the defensive composite instead of trend. Asks whether, once the universe is already calm, defensive RANKING still adds anything or whether the cap is the whole story.
